items.title: JNJ Stock Edges Up After-Hours On Apollo’s $20B Orthopedics Talks
items.summary: People familiar with the discussions told Bloomberg that Apollo is working toward a valuation of close to $20 billion for the unit, known as DePuy Synthes.

items.title: Is AbbVie Stock Actually Overpriced?
items.summary: AbbVie (ABBV) grew revenue 10.4% over the past twelve months and turned 33.9% of it into operating profit, second only to Eli Lilly among its peers on both counts. Its stock returned 24.9% over the same twelve months, fifth of the six. What the business delivered and what the market paid for it have come apart.

items.title: Is This BSX Stock Pullback Worth The Patience?
items.summary: Boston Scientific (BSX) trades at about $43, roughly 17% below the recent high it set on 19th Aug, 2026. Its own history with sharp drops is encouraging. That history does not cover a cyberattack it says is likely to hit its 2026 results, and the stock is down about 60% over the past twelve months. Start with the history.

items.title: Eli Lilly's Immunology Push Builds New Growth Engines Beyond GLP-1s
items.summary: LLY's immunology portfolio is gaining ground, with steady revenue growth, pipeline expansion and acquisitions broadening its next wave.

items.title: 3 Top Dividend Aristocrats To Own Near All-Time Highs
items.summary: Several Dividend Aristocrats, including Johnson & Johnson (JNJ), Coca-Cola (KO), and Exxon Mobil (XOM), are trading near all-time highs, reflecting bullish momentum driven by strong results or favorable operating conditions.

items.title: These 5 Dividend Stocks Survived 2008, COVID and Every Recession Before Them
items.summary: Chasing the fattest yield on the screen is a trap most income investors fall into, but a handful of companies have quietly raised their payouts through oil shocks, financial meltdowns, and a global pandemic without skipping a beat. The question is what they all have in common.

items.title: Merck Stock Vs. LLY: Why Is The Slower Grower More Expensive?
items.summary: In the high-stakes world of big pharma, the slower-growing giant now commands the higher price, forcing investors to decide what that premium is truly buying.
